title: GREMLIN: Generating Random Environments for Meta-Learning with Interacting Networks
abstract: arXiv:2611.33101v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Can randomly parameterized neural environments supply useful experience for learning a reinforcement learning algorithm? We investigate this question using DiscoRL's rule-discovery framework, replacing human-designed training games with sixteen selected neural environments. Each game combines bounded vector dynamics with a random strategy-based reward and an independent outcome reward. After 224.8 million agent-environment steps, we froze the teacher and trained fresh agents. DQN outscored GREMLIN on most games, both generated and human-designed. GREMLIN nevertheless outperformed the untrained teacher on all 26 games, showing that generated experience can improve a learning rule. It remains unclear whether this approach can yield a competitive rule with longer meta-training.

translated_title: GREMLIN：通过交互网络生成随机环境用于元学习
translated_abstract: 随机参数化的神经网络环境能否为学习强化学习算法提供有用的经验？我们使用 DiscoRL 的规则发现框架来研究这一问题，用十六个精选的神经环境替代人工设计的训练游戏。每个游戏将受限的向量动力学与基于随机策略的奖励以及独立的结局奖励相结合。在经过 2.248 亿步智能体-环境交互后，我们冻结了教师模型并训练了全新的智能体。DQN 在大多数游戏（无论是生成的还是人工设计的）上的得分超过了 GREMLIN。然而，GREMLIN 在全部 26 个游戏上都优于未经训练的教师模型，这表明生成的经验能够改进学习规则。该方法在更长时间的元训练下能否产生具有竞争力的规则仍不清楚。
tldr: 该研究提出 GREMLIN 方法，用随机参数化的神经网络环境替代人工设计游戏为元学习提供训练经验，实验证明生成的环境经验虽不及 DQN，但能在所有测试游戏上有效改进学习规则。
en_tdlr: GREMLIN replaces human-designed games with randomly parameterized neural environments for meta-learning, demonstrating that generated experience can improve a learning rule across all test games, though it does not yet outperform DQN.
